page: Google Cloud Platform c2d-standard-8 is a compute-optimized virtual machine instance powered by an AMD EPYC 7B13 processor. It features 8 vCPUs mapped to 4 physical cores with 2 threads per core on an x86_64 architecture. The instance is configured with 32.0 GB of dedicated RAM, providing a memory allocation of 4.0 GB per core. It does not include bundled local storage or integrated GPU hardware, and it offers zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

In benchmark evaluations, the c2d-standard-8 demonstrates strong single-core CPU performance, placing in the top 25% of tested instances via stress-ng. Multi-core CPU performance and memory bandwidth tests fall within the average range. Specifically, the instance achieves a stress-ng multi-core score of 11559.23 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 6531.0. Memory read-only bandwidth reaches 553.27 GB/sec for small cached blocks and 46.79 GB/sec for large uncached blocks. Static web serving throughput is measured at 10.68 GB/sec, while small-model LLM inference processes prompts at 499.45 tokens per second and generates text at 221.85 tokens per second.

This instance offers a balanced resource profile for compute-heavy workloads that do not require local NVMe storage or GPU acceleration. The dedicated CPU allocation ensures consistent execution times, making it qualitatively cost-efficient for steady-state processing. However, the lack of local storage requires reliance on network-attached storage, which may introduce latency tradeoffs. The server is well-suited for workloads such as software compilation, static web serving, light database operations, and small-scale language model inference.
